official.deadline_note: The New Zealand round published for Oxford entry 2027 ran 1 June 2026 to 4 August 2026 with decisions in November 2026; that closing date has passed and the next cycle's dates are not yet published.
official.application_cycle: Oxford entry 2027 (applications 1 June 2026 to 4 August 2026, decisions November 2026); the Rhodes Trust states applications reopen in 2027 for entry to Oxford in 2028
official.status_note: The Rhodes Trust states "Applications for the Rhodes Scholarship are now closed" and directs candidates to its mailing list to be notified when applications reopen in 2027 for entry to the University of Oxford in 2028.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Universities New Zealand states that fees are paid directly by the Trust to the College and University; the Rhodes Trust states the Scholarship covers University of Oxford course fees.
benefits: University of Oxford course fees, paid directly by the Trust to the College and University
Annual stipend of GBP 20,400 per annum (GBP 1,700 per month) for 2025-26, from which Scholars pay all living expenses including accommodation
Two economy class flights to and from the UK for the beginning and end of studies in Oxford
The fee required to apply to study at the University of Oxford, plus student visa fees and the International Health Surcharge
Settling in allowance on arrival, and assistance with visa renewal and IHS fees for a second course of study
Membership of the worldwide Rhodes Scholars community, with a Rhodes Scholarship Adviser at each New Zealand university
eligibility: On 1 August in the year of application hold New Zealand citizenship or a New Zealand Permanent Resident Visa
On 1 August in the year of application have spent at least five of the previous 10 years in New Zealand
By the time of entry to Oxford have graduated with an undergraduate degree with a GPA of 7.50/9.00
On 1 October 2026 be 18-24 and have not reached your 25th birthday (born after 1 October 2001 and on or before 2 October 2008)

Older candidates: on 1 October 2026 not have reached your 27th birthday (born after 1 October 1999) AND have met or will meet the academic requirements for completing a first undergraduate degree on or after 1 October 2025
requirements: Check eligibility through the Rhodes House eligibility checker before applying
Use the Rhodes House online application system for the New Zealand constituency
Ensure referees read the Guidance for Referees published by Universities New Zealand
Submit by the closing date published for the national constituency
documents: Completed online application via the Rhodes House application system
Referee reports (referees should read the Guidance for Referees published by Universities New Zealand)
Personal statements and evidence of leadership and activities, as specified by Rhodes House
selection_criteria: The application process and interview broadly address character, learning, and contribution (as described by a New Zealand Rhodes Scholar on the Universities New Zealand page)
coverage: University of Oxford course fees, paid directly by the Trust to the College and University
Annual stipend for living expenses, including accommodation - the Trust notes this is not sufficient to cover partners or dependents
Two economy class flights to and from the UK
Oxford application fee, student visa fees and International Health Surcharge
application_method: Check eligibility through the Rhodes House eligibility checker, then apply through the Rhodes House online application system
Contact the Rhodes Scholarship Adviser at your New Zealand university for support with the application
official.application_route: Apply through the Rhodes House online application system for the New Zealand constituency; Universities New Zealand - Te Pokai Tara administers the national application and selection process.
official.study_mode: Full-time postgraduate study at the University of Oxford
official.citizenship_residency: New Zealand citizenship or a New Zealand Permanent Resident Visa, plus at least five of the previous 10 years spent in New Zealand as at 1 August in the year of application
official.duration: Rhodes Scholars come to the UK for two or more years; up to three years of fees and stipend is available to Scholars who undertake a DPhil (PhD) at Oxford
official.description: The Rhodes Scholarship for New Zealand is a partnership between the Rhodes Trust and the Robertson Foundation, with the New Zealand application and selection process administered by Universities New Zealand - Te Pokai Tara. It is a fully-funded postgraduate award supporting outstanding all-round students to study at the University of Oxford, and up to three scholars are elected from New Zealand each year.

verification.notes: Universities New Zealand states the value is set by the Rhodes Trust; the stipend figure was taken from the Rhodes Trust's own Rhodes Scholarship page and is the most recent published figure (2025-26 academic year). The Rhodes Trust's application page confirms the round is closed and that applications reopen in 2027 for 2028 entry.

applicant_utility.summary: The Rhodes covers Oxford fees and an annual stipend of GBP 20,400, which the Trust explicitly says is not enough to support partners or dependents - plan your household finances around that single number before you commit. The binding constraints for most New Zealand applicants are the age rule and the five-of-the-last-ten-years residence test, both fixed to 1 August and 1 October in the year of application, so check them before you invest in the essay. Applications for the current cycle have closed; the Rhodes Trust says the next round opens in 2027 for Oxford entry in 2028, so use the coming months to line up referees and your adviser rather than waiting for the portal to open.
applicant_utility.best_fit: New Zealand citizens and Permanent Resident Visa holders with an outstanding undergraduate record, inside the age window, who have not yet begun a second degree and want postgraduate study at Oxford.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you meet the 1 August citizenship or PRV test and the five-of-the-previous-ten-years residence test in the year you will apply
Confirm your GPA of 7.50/9.00 or above will be achieved by the time you enter Oxford, not by the application deadline
Check which age limb you fall under - the standard 18-24 rule or the later-completed-first-degree exception tied to completing on or after 1 October 2025
Email the Rhodes Scholarship Adviser at your university early; their job is to encourage and support applications, and they can flag eligibility problems before you write
Send your referees the Universities New Zealand Guidance for Referees rather than letting them write blind
Budget for dependants separately - the Trust states the stipend does not cover partners or dependents
common_rejection_risks: Missing the five-of-the-previous-ten-years residence test, which catches applicants who grew up in New Zealand but spent long stretches overseas
Falling outside both age limbs, particularly applicants who finished their first degree late but not late enough for the exception
Applying before the 7.50/9.00 GPA is actually achieved, since the test is applied at the time of entry to Oxford
Referee reports that arrive late or generic - the Guidance for Referees exists precisely because this is a common failure point
Treating the Rhodes as a generic Oxford application: the selection conversation is about character, learning and contribution, not just academic results
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The Trust states the stipend is not sufficient to cover partners or dependents, so any family costs sit with you. The Oxford application fee, visa fees, the International Health Surcharge and two economy flights are covered, and a settling in allowance is provided, but day-to-day spending beyond accommodation and living expenses is on the Scholar.
document_audit: Referees must actually read the Guidance for Referees - Universities New Zealand publishes it specifically for this constituency and a generic reference weakens the file
Your academic record must convert to a 7.50/9.00 GPA by entry to Oxford, so order transcripts early and include the grading scale
Applications go through the Rhodes House system, not through Universities New Zealand directly - use the eligibility checker on the Rhodes House site first
alerts: Applications for the current round are closed; the Rhodes Trust says applications reopen in 2027 for entry to Oxford in 2028
Up to three scholars are elected from New Zealand each year, so the national round is highly selective before the Oxford-level comparison even begins
The Robertson Foundation partnership means the New Zealand constituency has its own administrator (Universities New Zealand), so use the New Zealand closing date rather than a generic Rhodes date
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Check eligibility on the Rhodes House site, apply through the Rhodes House online system for the New Zealand constituency, then Universities New Zealand runs the national selection with decisions in November.
